title: Six of eight modules were never wired into the loop. The benchmark was measuring the old pipeline.
the_question: 'you sure this is the smartest approach?' (asked three times)
the_answer: no -- not the grounding algorithm. The failure was one level up: NOTHING I BUILT WAS IN THE LOOP.

the_audit.reading: ten rounds of instruments, six of eight in a drawer. The runner still used text_locate_v1.best_run -- the regex matcher I had spent those rounds criticising.

why_every_number_was_flat: an improvement that is not connected cannot appear in any measurement. r84-r92 all reported 'the number did not move' while the code that was supposed to move it was never called. The instrument was measuring a pipeline I had already replaced on paper.
what_changed: page-first grounding is now called inside the loop, before the quoted-literal fallback, using the LIVE rendered DOM as the index.

measured_after_wiring.honest_caveat: SINGLE RUN. r78 measured a 1.73 stdev at a comparable configuration, so 21 must be repeated before it is claimed. It is the first number to exceed every prior record, including the pre-decline 18.

the_lesson.statement: building a better component is not progress. WIRING it is progress. Between the two there is a gap where ten rounds of real work produce zero behavioural change.
the_lesson.the_general_form: every claim of the shape 'the new approach is better' must be accompanied by the evidence that the new approach RAN. The runner now records `literal_source` and `grounding` on every task so this defect cannot recur silently.
the_lesson.law: no round may report on a module without a field in the run that proves the module executed
